masthead.kicker: Hidden Champions of India / a DeepThought series

headline.text: Infinita Biotech: a DSIR-recognized enzyme maker, in a market turning green — the margin hasn't caught up to the capability yet.

subhead.text: A Vadodara enzyme formulator exporting to 55+ countries, growing profit fast off a thin margin base.

p1_engine.eyebrow: A capability the margin hasn't caught up to

blocks.text: Revenue was ₹59.9 Cr in FY25, up 14.5% year-on-year, but the more striking number is profit growth: both net profit and EBITDA grew about 91% YoY off a small base — net margin is still thin at 3.35%, though ROCE (13.89%) is more solid.

It's a genuinely small, closely-held company — 93 employees as of August 2025, ₹6.25 lakh paid-up capital, directors Sonalben and Adarsh Alok Desai — with a real regulatory footprint for its size: DSIR-recognized R&D unit, ISO 9001:2008 certified, ZED Gold MSME certification.

It won India's National Startup Award (2022, Ministry of Commerce and Industry) and was runner-up for Most Innovative Company at ASSOCHAM's 9th MSME Excellence Awards (2023) — independent recognition, not just self-description.

The company claims presence in 55+ countries with 200+ enzyme products across 17+ industrial applications, but the only independently trackable export figure — a formal trade-shipment record — shows just $1.20M in tracked turnover over a full year (Dec 2024-Nov 2025), which likely undercounts total exports but is a much smaller number than the 55-country claim implies on its own.
blocks.source: company site (self-claimed) vs. exportgenius.in trade data

insights.point: The field is **mid-sized and growing steadily, with a wide estimate range.**
insights.evidence: Global industrial enzymes: $6.4-8.4B (2024/25) to $8.2-12B by 2030, 4.3-7.3%/yr depending on source.

insights.point: India's market is **smaller, faster-growing, and already concentrated.**
insights.evidence: India enzymes: $440.5M (2023), 7.8%/yr; industrial enzymes are 54.7% of that; the top players already hold 75%+ share, meaning Infinita competes in a market where a handful of firms dominate.

insights.point: The closest domestic peer is **roughly ten times its size.**
insights.evidence: Advanced Enzyme Technologies posted ₹637 Cr revenue (FY25) at 31% EBITDA margin and 10% ROE, present in 70+ countries — a scale-differentiated benchmark, not a direct peer, but it shows what margin looks like at scale in this category.

insights.point: The structural tailwind is **real and policy-backed.**
insights.evidence: Enzymes are being positioned as sustainable substitutes for harsh industrial chemicals (textile bleaching, pulp/paper, biodegradable detergents); cold-water detergent adoption in North America/Europe and EU green-chemistry policy both directly favor enzyme-based processing.

reflect.text: A small, independently-recognized, DSIR-backed enzyme maker growing profit fast off a thin margin, in a market a tenth of Advanced Enzyme's size is already navigating at 31% margin. The gap between the two is the whole opportunity.

p2_market.sourceNote: Market data: Precedence Research, GlobeNewswire, Grand View Research. Peer data: screener.in (Advanced Enzyme Technologies). marketSharePct not computed — Infinita's revenue is too small relative to the market range to produce a meaningful percentage.

p3_opportunities.lede: One clear place worth watching, visible in the gap between its export claim and its trackable trade data.

items.title: Closing the gap to Advanced Enzyme's margin
items.body: Advanced Enzyme Technologies runs at 31% EBITDA margin at ~10x Infinita's scale. Infinita's net margin is 3.35% despite fast profit growth — worth asking how much of that gap is scale economics that capacity growth alone would close, versus pricing/mix questions independent of scale.
items.source: Advanced Enzyme figures: screener.in. Infinita figures: Tofler.

guesslabel.text: Possibilities, not prescriptions. Which would work, and how much, only Infinita's own data and people can tell. Each is small, made to learn fast.

items.title: Break down margin by product line
items.body: Before assuming the margin gap is purely a scale story, break EBITDA margin down across the 200+ product portfolio for one quarter, and see whether a handful of applications are already close to Advanced Enzyme's margin while others are dragging the average down.

takeaway.text: A DSIR-recognized, award-winning enzyme maker growing profit at 91% a year off a margin a tenth of what the category leader gets. The gap itself is **the clearest number in this whole profile.**
